away.headline: Wisconsin and Penn State injury reports are headed in vastly different directions
away.blurb: Wisconsin and Penn State are set to take the field tomorrow in Happy Valley to get Big Ten play started. This season, the Big Ten is requiring each team to submit multiple availability reports for their conference games throughout the week leading up to the game. The first availability report for the two teams looked like a fairly similar list of players, with a handful of players in each category: out, questionable, and probable. Now, on the second submission, Wisconsin's is looking a lot healthier than Penn State's. Wisconsin's first report had 13 total players on it compared to 16 for Penn State. The Nittany Lions had nine listed as out, and Wisconsin only had four. Wisconsin listed five players as questionable, and Penn State had six. However, the newest report for Penn State now has 11 players listed as out and four as questionable, with only one player left as probable: Omarion Davis. That's in drastic contrast to Wisconsin's four as out and three as questionable, and now six as probable. And there are some important names on both of these two teams' lists. Malachi Coleman moving up from questionable to probable is maybe the biggest news on the Wisconsin side. He was a breakout star in Week 1 versus Notre Dame, but then was pulled out in the opening minutes of the Western Illinois game with a head injury. The fact that he's probable is huge news for Colton Joseph and Wisconsin. Abu Sama III also moved up from questionable to probable, but he was always going to play. He told reporters early in the week that he was 100% going to play. So his questionable status may have had more to do with reps than the actual likelihood of playing. Brock Riker is the starting center for Penn State, but he's most likely playing. His status as questionable, though, is something worth monitoring leading up to the game. A lot of the other injuries on Penn State's depth chart aren't as notable, and many are depth players and/or players who would have had moderate to low impact. The numbers are startling in comparison to each other, to see so many Nittany Lions out versus barely any for Wisconsin. The big names for Penn State are Howard, Granville, and Riker. For Wisconsin, missing Bates is a bummer, but having Sama, Coleman, Mandell, and Hilton back is huge. Notable Entries on Wisconsin and Penn State's availability report For Penn State, the big name is star sophomore wide receiver Koby Howard. He's arguably one of the most explosive wideouts in the Big Ten, and he's now on the mend for a few weeks. That's a big loss for the Nittany Lions, and they will have to look deeper on the depth chart for help. Max Granville is another name that's an important loss for Penn State. He was never going to play in this one, so it's not as notable in terms of current news, but it is notable if you didn't already know. He's an impact defensive lineman who could cause havoc. away.blurb: Penn State and Northwestern both put out their final Big Ten weekday availability reports before game day on Thursday night. What did we learn about Matt Campbell’s and David Braun’s teams 24 hours before the Nittany Lions clash with the Wildcats at 8 p.m. ET Friday on FOX? Starting with the visitors, top cornerback Daryus Dixson is still questionable. The second-year Nittany Lion appeared on Tuesday’s first report of the week as questionable. Speaking Wednesday morning, Campbell said that would be the case on that night’s report, and it indeed was. Beyond that, there is no other new news for the Lions. Kickoff specialist Cristiano Rosa is out and will not travel to Evanston. Lucas Tenbrock or Ryan Barker will handle kickoffs. Cornerback Christian Askew and linebacker Cam Smith are in the same boat. Top tight end Luke Dehnicke is now doubtful for the Wildcats. He’s a key part of their offense, so it’s obviously not good news for Northwestern. No. 2 receiver Hayden Eligon II is now probable, which is good news, of course. Top defensive back Braden Turner , who did not play last week, is also now doubtful as well. Another key cornerback, Josh Fussel , is now out. Another defensive back to monitor, Damon Walters , is now doubtful for Friday’s game. Last but not least, defensive tackle Troy Regovich could return to action. He is questionable. Most weeks, that will be Wednesday-Friday for head coach Matt Campbell’s team before a Saturday game. However, since this contest is Friday at 8 p.m. ET on FOX, the reports started on Tuesday. The final one then comes out two hours before kickoff. Northwestern is calling top tight end Luke Dehnicke questionable. The same goes for No. 2 receiver Hayden Eligon II and two of the team’s top tacklers, defensive backs Braden Turner and Damon Walters . More notable is that one of the team’s top corners, Josh Fussell , is doubtful to play. The No. 25-ranked Tigers will play No. 8 Florida, which currently ranks No. 5 in the FBS with 532.8 yards of total offense per game, on Saturday in Columbia. Smith and Kitchen were Mizzou's starting defensive ends in each of their first three games of the season, but over the past two game weeks, both players have left the field with injuries and were unable to return. Smith was helped off the field during the first half of Mizzou's Week 3 win over Troy due to an ankle injury. He attempted to return in the second half but only remained on the field for one play. The fifth-year senior did not play in MU's loss at Mississippi State this past Saturday. Kitchen came off the field during the first quarter of the game against the Bulldogs and was evaluated for a lower-body injury. He did not return to the field. "Both are doing the very best they can to get back," Drinkwitz said. "I doubt they can participate in much of any practice today (Tuesday), but both of those guys are experienced. You know, our protocol is you have to practice by Thursday in order to be available for the game. Life in the SEC, that's kind of how we go about it with guys who are questionable." away.headline: Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan
away.blurb: The Seminoles essentially have to win this weekend versus the Virginia Cavaliers to get their season back on track. Mike Norvell is coaching for his job, and the only real way to do that is by essentially winning out in ACC play. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. While both teams have a number of key players out, the focus for Florida State fans should be on the losses for Virginia on their defensive line. The biggest name to look for in that area is defensive tackle Jason Hammond. Hammond entered the season as one of the players with the most hype on the Virginia defensive front. This was supposed to be the year when Hammond finally took those next steps and solidified himself as one of the better linemen in the conference, but now it appears his return this season is in question. Kromah appears poised to remain the bell cow and should mostly see the opposing starters, but Wisner is where the lack of depth for Virginia will start to show itself. As the Cavaliers start to sub players out, FSU will try to spell Kromah with the equally-capable Wisner, and that is where FSU will need to force their will on a depleted opponent. The Wisner hype was perhaps a little too premature coming into the season based on his limited reps leading up to last week, but he has an easy path towards showing why the Seminoles put so much faith in him with a nice chunk of money on the transfer market. In the world of college football, teams will take whatever they can get if that gives them a chance to win. This is especially the case for a team like Florida State. Hammond absolutely leaves a hole on defense for the Cavaliers and his loss is further felt by the loss of depth across the front. Devon Baxter is the next most notable name to miss this weekend, largely a backup on the season, but several other depth players are also missing, leaving the Virginia rush defense susceptible. The good news for FSU is that their rushing attack is one of their biggest strengths, and Ousmane Kromah and Tre Wisner are more than up to the task . This game will still probably have some uphill sledding for the Noles to overcome, but this does at least display the obvious path for an FSU win and earn its first ACC win of the season. away.blurb: Virginia's defense is a solid, though far from outstanding, unit. But in a game where possessions are going to be limited, I question Florida State's ability to slow down the Cavaliers' offense enough for Ashton Daniels and company to keep up with them, given what they've shown over the first month of the season. That starts in the trenches, where Virginia appears to have a significant advantage over the Seminoles' undersized defensive line. Even if Florida State can come out firing as they did early against Alabama , the Cavaliers will stick to what has brought them success this season and wear down the Seminoles' front as the game rolls into the second half – where they could be hurt by play action from Pribula as the second level gets antsy trying to jump into the backfield. Which is exactly why I think Norvell comes out with a great plan and jumps on them early at home. Call it surprise, call it vibes, whatever it is, I feel it this week. I still believe this season takes a downturn fast from here, but this is one of the last wins they scrape out before it does. Slang that thing, Ashton. away.headline: Georgia Southern turns to Sun Belt play after three straight losses
away.blurb: Your Privacy Choices/(Opt-Out of Sale/Targeted Ads) Eagles open conference play at Coastal Carolina with a 1-3 record, plus key injury updates following Saturday’s loss to No. 25 Houston. Georgia Southern is ready to turn the page. The Eagles enter Sun Belt play at 1-3 after dropping three straight games, including Saturday’s 42-28 loss to No. 25 Houston at Allen E. Paulson Stadium. Despite the loss, Georgia Southern showed some encouraging signs offensively. Quarterback Max Johnson turned in his strongest performance of the season, completing 26 of 38 passes for 284 yards and a season-high three touchdowns without an interception. The Eagles also continued to expand the role of quarterback Weston Bryan. Georgia Southern used packages featuring both quarterbacks on the field together, including a flea-flicker that started with Bryan and ended with Johnson finding Alex Taylor for a 40-yard touchdown. Taylor finished with a season-high 119 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Georgia Southern now turns its attention to conference play while also dealing with several injuries. Head coach Clay Helton confirmed Monday that wide receiver Ashton Hollins will undergo season-ending shoulder surgery. Hollins, an Illinois transfer, suffered the injury in the Eagles’ loss at Jacksonville State. Inside linebacker Rashon Myles Jr. also left Saturday’s game against Houston with an Achilles injury. Helton said Myles was scheduled to undergo imaging Monday to determine the extent of the injury. The Eagles were also without two starting offensive tackles against Houston because of illness. Helton said neither had been medically cleared to play. Georgia Southern will now look to regroup as the Sun Belt portion of its schedule begins. The Eagles have lost three straight, while Coastal Carolina enters the matchup at 1-3 and riding a two-game losing streak. Both teams now look for a fresh start, 0-0 in conference play. Saturday will also mark Georgia Southern’s first matchup against the Chanticleers under first-year Coastal Carolina head coach Ryan Beard. The Eagles have won three straight games in the series, including a 26-6 victory in their last trip to Conway in 2024. Georgia Southern leads the all-time series 8-4. Georgia Southern and Coastal Carolina kick off Saturday, Oct. 3, at 7 p.m. from Brooks Stadium in Conway, South Carolina. away.headline: Why questionable weather wouldn't be so bad for Miami football against Clemson
away.blurb: This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/miami as Why Questionable Weather Wouldn't Be So Bad For Miami Football against Clemson . Weather delays are nothing that the Miami Hurricanes and Clemson Tigers have been immune to. Living in South Florida, one second the sky is pitch-black with hurricane-like weather; the next, it's sunny with people on the beach. The Tigers have faced weather delays throughout this season. Four games and three weather delays for the Tigers. It might be an advantage for anyone but the Hurricanes. Moreover, there could be a slight chance of another weather delay this weekend, given the amount of wet, warm weather the Tigers have had all season. It's something that Tigers head coach Dabo Swinney would love not to have to deal with again. "I just hope we can just play a regulation game and not have to have any delays or anything," Swinney said. Furthermore, the forecast doesn't favor a clean offensive showing that has been on display throughout the year. Miami ranks as the No. 1 overall offense in the country thanks to its passing attack led by Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney . Even with the most accurate arm in the country, weather can affect any passing attack and limit the Canes passing game. Miami will have to lean on its running game, and no better time than now. Miami wants to be a run-first team, but with the amount of talent on the outside, it's easy to see why they would lean away from it. Against Power Conference schools, the Hurricanes are averaging a little under 140 yards rushing per game. Great numbers, and overall, the Hurricanes are the second-best rushing team in the ACC through four games (behind Duke), but one thing has been lacking is the nasty yards behind the offensive line. This is a game to lean on Mark Fletcher Jr., Jordan Lyle, Girard Pringle Jr., and Javion Mallory. Even if they lean on Chris Wheatley-Humphrey , it would also be a breath of fresh air. Miami's running back room is deep, and this style of game can highlight how good Miami's offense is at all levels without CharMar Brown . "And that room, I said at the beginning of the year, and thank God that we have a talented running back room because that room's— my job is not easy, and it's a very physical job." offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson said. "And, I hate it for Marty, and, he's an awesome kid. I went and saw him last week in the hospital, and man, that's not easy. "But everybody is praying for him, loving him, rooting on him, and he's rooting us on. And, those guys are, in a way, playing a little bit more on an edge for him too. And so it's good to see those guys step up." Mensah will more than likely get his Heisman number to keep up with his campaign against Toney, Jerimah Smith, Trinidad Chamblish, and Kamario Taylor. home.blurb: After Wednesday night, during a traditional game week, we tend to find out a lot about what the Clemson Tigers are going to look like heading into their next matchup. Here’s what we found out about Clemson’s initial injury report heading into a contest with No. 4 Miami. In Clemson’s win out west against Cal, the team did it without cornerback Corian Gipson and defensive lineman Devarrick Woods. Gipson was “banged up” heading into the Tigers’ matchup with North Carolina and did not play. Meanwhile, he was questionable throughout the week against the Golden Bears, but he ultimately decided to remain sidelined. He has five total tackles on the season thus far and will look to change that against a high-powered Miami passing attack. However, the important takeaway is that Clemson should be full strength on defense with the pieces that aren’t out for the remainder of the season. Once again, he remains off the injury report, meaning he will be available to aid starter Tait Reynolds, if necessary. Key Offensive Lineman Remains Questionable In the win over Cal, left guard Elyjah Thurmon went down with an injury and did not return. Throughout the week, head coach Dabo Swinney said he was “day-to-day”. It seems like the junior will be the name this week that will be a game-time decision to be available. Clemson tends to have a player every game to be in this situation, and the guard will be the name we will be keeping an eye on for the next 48 hours. home.headline: Why questionable weather wouldn't be so bad for Miami football against Clemson
home.blurb: This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/miami as Why Questionable Weather Wouldn't Be So Bad For Miami Football against Clemson . Weather delays are nothing that the Miami Hurricanes and Clemson Tigers have been immune to. Living in South Florida, one second the sky is pitch-black with hurricane-like weather; the next, it's sunny with people on the beach. The Tigers have faced weather delays throughout this season. Four games and three weather delays for the Tigers. It might be an advantage for anyone but the Hurricanes. Moreover, there could be a slight chance of another weather delay this weekend, given the amount of wet, warm weather the Tigers have had all season. It's something that Tigers head coach Dabo Swinney would love not to have to deal with again. "I just hope we can just play a regulation game and not have to have any delays or anything," Swinney said. Furthermore, the forecast doesn't favor a clean offensive showing that has been on display throughout the year. Miami ranks as the No. 1 overall offense in the country thanks to its passing attack led by Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney . Even with the most accurate arm in the country, weather can affect any passing attack and limit the Canes passing game. Miami will have to lean on its running game, and no better time than now. Miami wants to be a run-first team, but with the amount of talent on the outside, it's easy to see why they would lean away from it. Against Power Conference schools, the Hurricanes are averaging a little under 140 yards rushing per game. Great numbers, and overall, the Hurricanes are the second-best rushing team in the ACC through four games (behind Duke), but one thing has been lacking is the nasty yards behind the offensive line. This is a game to lean on Mark Fletcher Jr., Jordan Lyle, Girard Pringle Jr., and Javion Mallory. Even if they lean on Chris Wheatley-Humphrey , it would also be a breath of fresh air. Miami's running back room is deep, and this style of game can highlight how good Miami's offense is at all levels without CharMar Brown . "And that room, I said at the beginning of the year, and thank God that we have a talented running back room because that room's— my job is not easy, and it's a very physical job." offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson said. "And, I hate it for Marty, and, he's an awesome kid. I went and saw him last week in the hospital, and man, that's not easy. "But everybody is praying for him, loving him, rooting on him, and he's rooting us on. And, those guys are, in a way, playing a little bit more on an edge for him too. And so it's good to see those guys step up." Mensah will more than likely get his Heisman number to keep up with his campaign against Toney, Jerimah Smith, Trinidad Chamblish, and Kamario Taylor.
